first_hunter_context.bar: Company guide: Q3 2026 adjusted EBITDA 'approximately $575 million', shipments +~300kt vs Q2's 4.025Mt (>4.3Mt), ASP +$55/t vs Q2's $1,124 (8-K ex-99.1 2026-07-23, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000764065/000076406526000097/clf-202606308xkex991.htm; call: https://www.manufacturingdive.com/news/cleveland-cliffs-offers-bright-q3-2026-outlook-despite-maintenance-outages/826130/). Street: revenue ~$5.72B (sweep and https://www.benzinga.com/node/62267494 agree), EPS $0.19-0.25 across sources (Benzinga $0.24, opencapital $0.25, sweep $0.19-0.24). The guide-implied revenue (4.3Mt x ~$1,179 plus ~$0.7B non-steel) is ~$5.8B, ~1-2% above the $5.72B consensus, which is the basis of print_vs_bar.
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest 78.52M shares at the 2026-09-30 FINRA settlement, ~13.8% of shares outstanding, 4.67 days to cover (https://equibles.com/stocks/clf/shortinterest, fetched 2026-10-16 by the sweep; the 10-15 settlement is not published until ~10-24). Baseline skew -12.48 vol points (upside paid), put/call OI 0.59, ATM IV 104.5%, event-implied move 10.5%. Tape: 20d -2.4%, 5d -6.0%; CLF closed 12.19 (10-08) -> 12.98 (10-09, +6.5% on 24.8M shares) -> 12.86 (10-13) -> 12.58 (10-14) -> 12.15 (10-15, -3.4% on 24.3M) while STLD went 234.17 -> 240.76 and NUE 246.14 -> 254.69 over the same sessions (Yahoo chart v8, https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/CLF?range=1mo&interval=1d). Both legs are CLF-specific and no news attaches to either. A 13.8% short with upside-paid skew says a positive guide would squeeze; a negative needs to explain why that mechanism fails.

evidence.text: US HRC spot rose through the whole of Q3 and into Q4: Nucor's weekly CSP went from $1,190/st (2026-09-08) to $1,220 (09-28) to $1,230 (10-05) with lead times held at 3-5 weeks, SMU's average was $1,225/st on 09-08 and Kallanish put domestic HRC at $1,210-1,220/st on 10-02, against the ~$1,150/t level CLF's July call cited; the Q2 release said Q4 EBITDA will 'even further exceed' the ~$575M Q3 guide, and a higher Q4 number than the July framing is what the spot series implies.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last print (2026-07-23, +15.98%) rose on the Q3 EBITDA guide despite an EPS miss (https://finviz.com/news/371803/cleveland-cliffs-shares-jump-as-upbeat-third-quarter-forecast-outweighs-earnings-miss-nyse-clf); 2025-10-20 +21.47% and 2026-02-09 -16.43% were also guide-driven. This name pays, in both directions, on the forward guide.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the skew is upside-paid (-12.5) and Wells Fargo upgraded on 10-06 on exactly this logic. Not fully priced: 13 analysts sit at Hold with a $12.60 mean target against a $12.15 spot (https://ca.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/CLEVELAND-CLIFFS-INC-50916560/consensus/), the stock is 24.6% off its high and gave back its whole pre-print rally in the two sessions before the seal; if the market held a Q4 guide materially above $575M the stock would not be sitting on a mean target 4% away.
evidence.independence: Nucor's 2026-09-17 Q3 guide cites 'higher average selling prices and stable volumes' at steel mills (https://www.steelorbis.com/steel-news/latest-news/nucor-issues-q3-2026-earnings-guidance-expects-higher-steel-mills-and-steel-products-earnings-1478837.htm); Steel Dynamics' 2026-09-17 guide expects 'average realized steel selling values to increase' and says low customer inventories 'continue to support favorable pricing conditions' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001022671/000110465926108777/tm2625690d1_ex99-1.htm); Wells Fargo 2026-10-06 OW/$14 on 2027 EBITDA $2.65B above consensus (https://www.itiger.com/news/1196432764).

evidence.text: Both EAF peers' mid-quarter guides (2026-09-17) missed consensus on costs: Nucor guided $5.55-5.65 vs ~$6.17 citing 'higher costs of products sold' and no repeat of a $130M Q2 refund, Steel Dynamics $5.34-5.38 vs ~$5.99, and both fell ~5% on the day; CLF's July guide assumed 'slightly lower' Q3 costs, so a cost-side miss against the $575M is the live risk the peers flag.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-04-20 (-2.11%) fell on an $80M energy-cost spike despite a beat (https://insights.munich-startup.de/news/feed/cleveland-cliffs-shares-drop-5-despite-q1-earnings-beat-as-80m-energy-cost-spike-weighs-on-profitability); a cost miss on the reported quarter has been sold before, but modestly.
evidence.why_not_priced: The peer guides are a month old and the steel group has since recovered (NUE 236 -> 255, STLD 226 -> 241 from 10-01); CLF's own consensus EPS ($0.19-0.25) still brackets the guide-implied number, so nobody has cut for costs. Proxy: CLF is integrated with its own iron ore and does not buy scrap at Nucor's scale, so the transmission is partial and the company has not confirmed it.
evidence.independence: Steel Dynamics 8-K 2026-09-17 says fabrication margins were hit by 'increased steel input material costs' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001022671/000110465926108777/tm2625690d1_ex99-1.htm). STLD reports after the close on 2026-10-19, inside this window, so its actual cost line lands on the 10-20 session.

evidence.text: Stelco is indefinitely idling its Hamilton cold-rolled and coated lines from 2026-10-09 (350-500 layoffs), its president's 2026-10-09 letter to Ottawa says continued production of those products is loss-making with demand down ~25% vs the 2024 quarterly average and Canadian CR/coated exports to the US down 58%, Canada's industry minister has threatened court action under the Investment Canada Act with her lawyers 'reviewing' the reply and the CEO saying he will fight it in court; the July release had said Stelco was 'positioned to return to generating significant earnings', so the Stelco contribution inside the $575M and the Q4 guide is weaker than July framed, and a restructuring charge or a Canadian filing could land in the window.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The idling itself cost the stock 9% on 2026-09-28 (https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/09/28/cleveland-cliffs-sinks-9-as-selloff-outruns-steel-group-nucor-and-steel-dynamics-pull-back/) and was recovered by 10-05 (+10%); Stelco commentary on prior prints has not been the line the stock traded on.
evidence.why_not_priced: The idling announcement is priced (the 9% drop and the recovery). What is not: no 8-K has been filed and no charge has been quantified, the company says tonnage is unchanged but has not said what the Q3 Stelco EBITDA was, and the government's legal decision has no date. Sized net of the rest of the company: Stelco is roughly 15% of shipments and the idled lines are a fraction of that, while the US mills carry the quarter; the 13.8% short and upside-paid skew argue for keeping this small.
evidence.independence: Algoma Steel's 2026-10-01 Q3 guide: shipments ~145kt and adjusted EBITDA C$-10M to C$-20M, mostly a power outage but with 'a less favourable sales mix' (https://www.steelorbis.com/steel-news/latest-news/algoma-steel-expects-negative-adjusted-ebitda-in-q3-on-power-outage-impact-1481453.htm); company announcement of the idling 2026-09-29 (https://www.miningweekly.com/article/cleveland-cliffs-to-idle-output-at-canada-steel-plant-blames-tariffs-2026-09-29); minister's five-day deadline (https://www.insauga.com/industry-minister-presses-stelcos-u-s-owner-to-present-job-saving-plan-in-5-days/).

evidence.text: Detroit-three Q3 2026 US sales were weak (GM 670,974, -6%; Ford 509,764, -6.6%; Stellantis 324,277, flat) and Omdia's North American Q3 production tracker ran about -0.6% y/y, while CLF's July guide assigned about half of its ~300kt sequential Q3 shipment increase to automotive (29% of Q2 steelmaking revenue).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Automotive volume has not been the line prior prints traded on; Q2's auto shipments were the highest in two years and the stock still traded on the guide.
evidence.why_not_priced: Proxy, not a company number: the sequential increase CLF guided is against a Q2 depressed by April-May outages, so a y/y sales decline does not refute it, and the company's own statement (Q2 auto shipments highest in two years, finishing lines 'full') is the more direct series and points the other way. Filed small for that reason.
evidence.independence: Omdia July 2026 tracker: 3Q output 'pacing lower' (https://omdia.tech.informa.com/om145787/north-america-vehicle-production-tracker-3q--july-2026); CLF call 2026-07-23 for the automotive share of the shipment increase (https://www.industryweek.com/leadership/companies-executives/news/55393737/cleveland-cliffs-sees-much-stronger-second-half-more-growth-into-27).

evidence.text: Management said on the Q2 call that resetting fixed-price (largely automotive) contracts signed at ~$800/t to the ~$1,150/t-plus market is 'a foregone conclusion' worth about $500M of EBITDA year over year and that 2027 adjusted EBITDA could reach $3.3B; the Q3 call is the first since contract negotiations for 2027 began and a quantified 2027 reset is the kind of line this name has paid for.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Forward-year framing moved the stock on 2026-02-09 (-16.43%, '26 outlook below expectations) and 2026-07-23 (+15.98%); the name trades on the forward number.
evidence.why_not_priced: The $3.3B figure is three months old and the mean target is $12.60 on a Hold consensus, so the Street has not underwritten it; Wells Fargo's 10-06 upgrade ($2.65B 2027 EBITDA 'above FactSet consensus', $500M from contract repricing) is the only house that has, and it moved the stock ~1%. If a dated, quantified reset were in the price the consensus 2027 number would already sit near $2.65B.
evidence.independence: Wells Fargo 2026-10-06 (https://www.itiger.com/news/1196432764). Note this finding and finding 1 both rest on HRC being higher than July assumed; they are different lines (Q4 guide vs 2027 contracts) but not independent evidence.

evidence.text: CLF-specific tape into the print: +6.5% on 2026-10-09 (24.8M shares) with no news, then -2.2% and -3.4% on 10-14/10-15 (24M shares) while NUE and STLD rose, leaving the stock at 12.15-12.20 with 78.5M shares (13.8%) short, 4.67 days to cover and options skew paying for upside.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The two largest prior up-moves (+21.47% 2025-10-20, +15.98% 2026-07-23) came into a stock that was heavily shorted; the squeeze is a mechanism of its own on this name.
evidence.why_not_priced: The pre-print rally has been unwound, so there is less to sell on a merely in-line print; the short base has not covered (last settlement 09-30). An unexplained move is not evidence of direction and is sized near zero; the positioning facts are what carry the small positive.
evidence.independence: Short interest from https://equibles.com/stocks/clf/shortinterest (2026-09-30 settlement); peer closes from https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/STLD?range=1mo&interval=1d and https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/NUE?range=1mo&interval=1d.

evidence.text: Two new capital projects since the last print: a $1B Middletown Works investment backed by a $500M DOE award (2026-08-21) and a $200M Butler Works GOES expansion with a $75M DOE award showcased to the Energy Secretary on 2026-10-06; the 2026 capex guide is still ~$700M and a 2027 capex frame above that, if given on the call, would weigh on the free-cash-flow and sub-2.5x leverage story the stock is partly valued on.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-04-20 (-2.11%) traded partly on $7.25B of long-term debt and negative FCF (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/cleveland-cliffs-drops-5-despite-142748272.html); the balance sheet is a line this stock has sold on.
evidence.why_not_priced: Both announcements are public and the DOE share is grant money, so most of this is priced; what is not is a 2027 capex number, which the company usually gives in February rather than October, hence the small size.
evidence.independence: Company release list (https://www.clevelandcliffs.com/news/news-releases) for the 2026-08-21 Middletown and 2026-10-05 Butler items; 2026 capex guide of ~$700M in the Q2 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000764065/000076406526000097/clf-202606308xkex991.htm).

evidence.text: AISI raw steel output for the week ending 2026-10-10 was 1.796Mt at 77.8% utilisation, +4.1% y/y, with year-to-date production +5.3% at 79.0% average utilisation and the Great Lakes region (CLF's core) at 534kt; industry volume ran above last year through the whole of Q3, consistent with CLF's >4.3Mt shipment guide.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Shipment volume alone has not been the line prior prints traded on.
evidence.why_not_priced: Industry proxy, published weekly and widely read; it corroborates the guide rather than beating it, so it carries little size.
evidence.independence: Scrap Monster report of the same AISI release (https://www.scrapmonster.com/news/steel/u.s.-raw-steel-production-report-output-up-4.1-yoy-aisi-2026-10-13/100236); Steel Dynamics guided 'record shipments' for Q3 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001022671/000110465926108777/tm2625690d1_ex99-1.htm).

evidence.text: Nucor reports Q3 after the close on 2026-10-26, the first full peer print on sheet pricing and costs after CLF's; its read-through lands a week after this window.
The FINRA 2026-10-15 short-interest settlement (whether the 78.5M short base built or covered into the print) is published around 2026-10-24.
Wells Fargo upgrade to Overweight, target $14 (2026-10-06), as a finding of its own
Cleveland-Cliffs +8-10% on 2026-10-05 as 'Stelco fallout fades'
Quiver 'Cleveland-Cliffs slides 4.3% as traders fade a recent tariff-driven rally' as the cause of the 10-14/15 drop
Argus 'US HRC prices jump as October availability limited' as an October 2026 price print
SMU average HRC 'approaching $1,300/st' as of 2026-09-22
Earnings date of 2026-10-26 (Investing.com, EarningsWhispers)
No cause found for the CLF-specific +6.5% on 2026-10-09 or the -5.5% over 2026-10-14/15 (news searches by date, analyst-action searches, Quiver items: the 'slides 4.3%' piece is dated 2026-06-08).

No 8-K since the 07-24 item 5.02 (CFO promoted to President): EDGAR submissions show only an SD (09-18), a 13G (08-07) and two Form 4s on 10-02, both director retainer share elections (Bloom, Cronin; 3,487 shares each at $11.47), not open-market trades.
No POSCO definitive agreement or asset-sale (Toledo HBI, FPT) news since the July call said no deal was imminent on valuation.
No October 2026 US-Canada or US-Mexico Section 232 deal; latest reporting is August talks with no agreement.
No published Q3 adjusted EBITDA consensus (FactSet/Visible Alpha/TIKR) reachable; the $575M guide is the only EBITDA bar.

No Nucor CSP letter for 2026-10-12 found; the series ends at $1,230 on 10-05. No SMU/Argus/Fastmarkets HRC assessment for 10-13 to 10-16 reachable (mysteel price cells blank, nasdaq/benzinga pages 403/503).
No October 2026 analyst preview beyond the Wells Fargo 10-06 upgrade; no downgrade in the week before the print.
No Canadian court filing against Cleveland-Cliffs as of 2026-10-13 reporting; the minister's office said lawyers were reviewing the 10-09 letter.

first_hunter_context.bar: Book value per common share $12.90 at 2026-06-30 (company Q2 release, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000826675/000082667526000074/a2q26earningsrelease.htm). The market's implied Q3 bar is derived, not published: spot $10.89 is 0.844x June BV, and KBW ($15 -> $12.50, 2026-10-07) and BTIG ($14.50 -> $12.00, 2026-10-06) cut targets ~17%, so the street sits near a -15% to -17% BV decline (~$10.75-11.00). EPS bar is single-sourced (Benzinga non-GAAP $0.53, revenue $104.6M), so the EPS finding is capped small.
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest 17.54M shares at the 2026-09-30 FINRA settlement, 7.1% of shares outstanding, 2.15 days to cover (Equibles, https://equibles.com/stocks/dx/shortinterest, fetched 2026-10-16), up from ~10.4M / 4.2% of float / 1.6 DTC at the 2026-08-21 snapshot on the same page: shorts built ~70% into the print but 7% is not crowded. Option chain unusable (ATM spread 120% of mid, 1,866 total OI, put/call OI 1.09), so no skew statement exists. Stock sits 3% off its 52-week low, -10.6% over 20 days.

evidence.text: Two Agency-only peers pre-announced September-30 book value down ~16% in Q3: Orchid Island $6.02 vs $7.22 at June 30 (-16.6%, total return on equity -12.5%, 8-K 2026-10-14) and Invesco Mortgage Capital $6.74 vs $8.03 (-16.1%; monthly path $7.75 at Jul 31, $7.74 at Aug 31, so -12.9% in September alone). Both were ~100% notional-hedged (ORC hedges $10.25B vs $10.36B repo; IVR $6.8B vs $6.8B repo). DX at June 30 carried $14.09B swaps + $4.26B Treasury futures (+$0.75B swaptions) against $23.2B of liabilities, ~79-82% hedged, at 8.1x leverage; in Q1 2026, the last spread-widening quarter, DX's BV fell 6.3% vs ORC -6.1% and AGNC -5.6%. The 10-year rose from 4.42% (Jun 30) to 5.29% (Sep 30) and Agency MBS posted ~-96bp of excess return in September. Read-through: DX Sept-30 BV about $10.3-11.0 (-15% to -20%) vs $12.90; the market-implied bar is ~$10.75-11.00, so the lower hedge ratio puts the central estimate at or slightly below the bar.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Baseline: seven prints, median |move| 0.81%, max 1.8%. The Q1 2026 print (BV -6.3%, the largest decline in the set) moved +0.81%; the Q2 2026 print (BV +2.4%) moved -1.58%. The stock prices BV intra-quarter and the print itself has moved little.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the stock is -18.6% since the July print and -15.5% from $12.89 on Sep 8, to 1.0x the peer-implied BV. What is not visibly priced is the hedge-ratio gap: if the market expected DX to print worse than the ~100%-hedged peers, the stock would sit below ~$10.5 (a discount to the implied book), and the sell-side would not be holding Buy/Outperform with targets 10-15% above spot.
evidence.independence: IVR 8-Ks: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001437071/000143707126000076/ivr10142026-8kxex991.htm (2026-10-14), https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001437071/000143707126000073/ivr09152026-8kxex991.htm (2026-09-15), https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001437071/000143707126000067/ivr08142026-8kxex991.htm (2026-08-14), IVR June 30 BV $8.03 from https://www.barchart.com/story/news/3561142/invesco-mortgage-capital-inc-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial-results. DX hedge book and leverage from the Q2 release (company document). DX Q1 2026 BV walk from https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/826675/000082667526000035/a1q26earningsrelease.htm. September MBS excess return -96bp (Fidelity, https://institutional.fidelity.com/app/proxy/content?literatureURL=%2F931730.PDF) and MBS-Treasury spread +13bp to 125bp (AGNC data via https://ph.investing.com/news/economy-news/us-treasury-yields-surge-putting-a-chain-reaction-in-focus-2625092). 10-year 4.42% on 2026-06-30 (https://www.morningstar.com/news/dow-jones/202606307321/10-year-treasury-yield-rises-to-4420-data-talk) and 5.29% on 2026-09-30 (https://www.mortgagenewsdaily.com/treasury/10yr). This is a peer-and-sensitivity proxy for DX's own number; DX's 10-Q Item 3 sensitivity table could not be read (SEC render truncated, mirror 403).

evidence.text: DX discloses an intra-quarter book value on its call (Q2 call, July 20: 'The book value as of Friday was $12.67', i.e. -1.8% from June 30 by July 17). Since the Sept 30 quarter-end the 10-year has fallen from 5.29% to ~5.09% (Oct 15 close, -11bp on the day; H.15 shows 5.22/5.24/5.21/5.19 for Oct 8-14) and the Agency MBS basis tightened from a one-year high set early in the week of Oct 12 (Nuveen weekly). An Oct 16 'book value as of Friday' several percent above the Sept 30 figure will be stated on the 10:00 ET call, inside the window, alongside a Sept-30 print the peers have already framed.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No direct history: the July 17 figure given on the Q2 call was below the June 30 BV and the stock moved -1.58% that day. Peers' Sept-30 8-Ks (ORC, IVR) gave no October-to-date figure, so DX's would be the first October mark from an Agency mREIT.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock has risen ~3% from its Oct 7 close of $10.57 (10-year 5.22%) to $10.89 as the 10-year fell to 5.09%. If the market had fully priced an October BV recovery of 3-5% on top of a -16% Sept-30 print, the stock would be nearer $11.2-11.4 (1.0x the recovered book) rather than $10.89.
evidence.independence: Rates: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/15/us-treasury-yields-investors-economic-data-.html (2026-10-15), https://www.federalreserve.gov/releases/h15/ (H.15, 2026-10-15), https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/government-bond-yield. MBS basis: https://www.nuveen.com/global/insights/fixed-income/fixed-income-weekly-commentary (week of ~2026-10-12). Oct 7 price $10.57 from https://www.google.com/finance/labs/quote/DX:NYSE. This is a rates-to-book-value proxy; the company has not published an October figure.

evidence.text: Short interest rose from ~10.4M shares (4.2% of float, 1.6 days to cover) at the Aug 21 snapshot to 17.54M (7.1% of shares outstanding, 2.15 days to cover) at the Sept 30 FINRA settlement, a ~70% build into the print, with no usable option chain to hedge in (ATM spread 120% of mid, 1,866 contracts OI).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No instance in the seven-print baseline where positioning visibly drove the reaction; all seven moves were under 2%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The build is recent (settlements of Sep 15 and Sep 30, published early October) and small in absolute terms; if a squeeze were being priced the stock would not sit 3% off its 52-week low. At 7% of shares and 2 days to cover it is a mild mechanism, not a crowded short.
evidence.independence: Baseline options block: put/call OI 1.09, total OI 1,866 (sealed 2026-10-16). None from a second short-interest source; Benzinga's undated 5.75M figure conflicts and was rejected.

evidence.text: DX priced $120M of 9.375% Series D cumulative preferred on Sep 22 (4.8M shares at $25, net ~$115.9M, 720k-share greenshoe, closed Sep 29; common closed $12.07 on Sep 21 per the $6.035 share-cap in the prospectus) with stated use of proceeds 'to finance the acquisition of Agency and other investment securities'. The money buys Agency MBS at the widest spreads in a year (basis 125bp at Sept 30) rather than funding a de-leveraging; it also costs ~$11.3M/yr of preferred dividends (~$0.045/common share) and ~$4M of issuance cost (~$0.02/share of BV), and tells the market management chose to hold or add risk through the September selloff.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Prior capital raises were common ATM issuance ($442M in Q1, $391M in Q2) described by management as accretive; neither print moved more than 1.6%. No prior preferred issuance in the baseline window.
evidence.why_not_priced: The raise itself is public and priced (stock fell $12.07 -> $11.18 from Sep 21 to Sep 25, coinciding with the 10-year hitting 5.2%). What the print adds is whether the capital was deployed at wide spreads (raising forward NII per share) or held as liquidity; the 42c of Q2 NII against a 51c dividend makes that the live question on the call.

evidence.text: PNC, reporting 2026-10-15, delivered Q3 NII of $4,206M, +$99M or +2.4% q/q against its own guide of +3-3.5% from a $4,107M base, with NIM down 2bp to 2.94% 'partially offset by increased funding costs'; Fifth Third's unchanged Q3 guide is NII +2-2.5% from $2.22B (i.e. $2.264-2.276B) and the July call said deposit costs would be 'stable to maybe slightly up', so a peer that just missed its own NII guide on funding costs points to the low end for FITB. Truist (2026-10-16) landed NII +1.1% inside its +1-1.5% guide and JPMorgan raised its 2026 NII outlook, so the broader peer read is mixed and this is sized as a proxy.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-07-17): NII $2.22B, NIM +6bp, FY NII guide raised, adjusted EPS $1.02 vs $0.98 consensus, stock -2.29%; the name did not pay for an NII beat last time, so a small NII shortfall is also likely to be damped.
evidence.why_not_priced: PNC reported after Fifth Third last spoke (09-15); FITB's 5-day run-up is only -0.64% through the big-bank prints and consensus revenue ($3.34B) still sits on the guide's midpoint, so the funding-cost shortfall at a peer has not moved FITB's bar. If it had, the whisper would be at or below consensus rather than $0.03 above it.
evidence.independence: Proxy, not a company number.
